To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. MCMC sampling in the latent space of a generative model can mix well in the data space; 2. MCMC in the latent space can traverse modes in the data; and 3. MCMC with a generative model in the latent space as a backbone can learn energy-based models with proper sampling.

(1) the EBM is the exponential tilting of a latent variable model; (2) MCMC sampling in the latent space can be used to sample EBM; (3) MCMC in the latent space is mixing and thus can be used for learning EBMs; and (4) the EBM has a simple form in the latent space.

we can learn an energy-based model with a flow-based generative model as a backbone, and MCMM sampling in the latent space of the flow-based generative models mixes and traverses modes of the EBM, so that the learned EBM can serve as an energy-based prior for variational inference.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new learning algorithm for EBM that is theoretically well-founded and empirically effective.
the following two questions: (1) How can we sample from an energy-based model? (2) How can we learn an energy-based model with a latent variable model as a backbone?
the following questions: 1) how to learn EBMs in high-dimension data space, and 2) how to sample from EBMs in high dimension data space.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have proposed a new way to learn energy-based model (E-BM).

we propose to use a latent variable model (e.g., a flow-based model) to learn the energy function (e.g., the deep network) and the energy function (the deep network) to learn the latent space of the latent variable model (i.e., the flow-based model).
we can now sample from energy-based models, and learn them, in a way that mixes well and explores modes in high-dimensional data spaces.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, we propose a new EBM learning algorithm, which learns a latent variable model as a backbone, and the EBM is defined as a correction or an exponentially tilting of the backbone model.
we propose a new EBM with a simple and elegant form, which can be efficiently learned by MCMC sampling.
we learn a flow-based model, which can be learned by MCMC, and use it to learn an EBM, which also can be learned by the same MCMC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
learning EBM with a latent space that mixes well is a promising way to learn EBMs in practice.
learning an EBM with a well-mixing latent space MCMC is a promising direction for both theory and applications of EBMs.
MCMC mixing in the latent space can be much easier than that in the data space, and it is a good practice to learn the EBM in latent space, and then map back to data space for inference.
